intro: What's up, soccer fans! Today we've got twenty-five crazy soccer facts that you've probably never heard before. Stolen trophies, psychic octopuses, and a match that ended one hundred forty-nine to zero! Stick around until the very end, because the last one is totally unbelievable. Let's kick it off!
outro: And that's all twenty-five! Which fact surprised you the most? Tell me in the comments! Check out one of these videos next, and don't forget to subscribe for more crazy facts. See you next time!

facts.title: The oldest club in the world
facts.narration: Fact number one! The oldest soccer club in the world is Sheffield FC, in England. It was founded way back in eighteen fifty-seven, and FIFA officially recognizes it as the oldest club on the planet. It's still playing today, more than one hundred sixty years later!

facts.title: No two fields are the same
facts.narration: Fact number two! Soccer fields don't all have the same size. The rules allow a pitch to be anywhere from ninety to one hundred twenty meters long. That's why some stadiums feel huge, and others feel super tight!

facts.title: Where did the time go?
facts.narration: Fact number three! A soccer match lasts ninety minutes, but the ball is only in play for about fifty-five to sixty of them. The rest of the time goes to throw-ins, free kicks, fouls, and players rolling on the grass!

facts.title: The goalkeeper who invented the penalty
facts.narration: Fact number four! The penalty kick was invented by an Irish goalkeeper named William McCrum. He came up with the idea, and it became part of the official rules in eighteen ninety-one. A goalkeeper invented the scariest moment for goalkeepers!

facts.title: Hands everywhere!
facts.narration: Fact number five! Until nineteen twelve, goalkeepers could use their hands anywhere in their own half of the field. Imagine a keeper running to midfield and catching the ball! The rule was changed so they could only use their hands inside the penalty area.

facts.title: Cards inspired by traffic lights
facts.narration: Fact number six! Yellow and red cards were invented by an English referee named Ken Aston. He got the idea while waiting at a traffic light. Yellow means slow down, and red means stop! The cards were first used at the nineteen seventy World Cup.

facts.title: The first World Cup
facts.narration: Fact number seven! The first World Cup was played in Uruguay in nineteen thirty, and only thirteen teams took part. In the final, Uruguay and Argentina couldn't agree on which ball to use, so they used Argentina's ball in the first half and Uruguay's ball in the second. Uruguay won four to two!

facts.title: A ball made for TV
facts.narration: Fact number eight! The classic black and white soccer ball was made famous by the Telstar, the official ball of the nineteen seventy World Cup. It had black and white panels so it would be easier to see on black and white TVs! The name Telstar even means television star.

facts.title: The trophy under the bed
facts.narration: Fact number nine! During World War Two, the original World Cup trophy, called the Jules Rimet Trophy, was in danger. So Ottorino Barassi, an Italian official, hid it in a shoebox under his bed to keep it safe. The most famous trophy in the world, sleeping under a bed!

facts.title: Saved by a dog
facts.narration: Fact number ten! In nineteen sixty-six, just months before the World Cup in England, the Jules Rimet Trophy was stolen. A week later, a dog named Pickles found it wrapped in newspaper under a hedge in London! Pickles became a national hero.

facts.title: Stolen again… forever
facts.narration: Fact number eleven! Brazil got to keep the Jules Rimet Trophy after winning their third World Cup. But in nineteen eighty-three, it was stolen again in Rio de Janeiro. This time there was no Pickles to save the day. It was never found, and many people believe it was melted down!

facts.title: Never missed one
facts.narration: Fact number twelve! Brazil is the only country that has played in every single World Cup ever held. They also have the most titles, with five World Cup trophies. No wonder they call it the country of soccer!

facts.title: The silence of the Maracanã
facts.narration: Fact number thirteen! In nineteen fifty, around two hundred thousand fans packed the Maracanã stadium in Rio to watch Brazil play Uruguay. Brazil only needed a draw to win the World Cup. But Uruguay won two to one, and the stadium went completely silent. Brazilians still call it the Maracanazo!

facts.title: A champion at 17
facts.narration: Fact number fourteen! Pelé was just seventeen years old when he won the nineteen fifty-eight World Cup with Brazil. He scored two goals in the final, and then he cried on his teammates' shoulders. He was still a teenager!

facts.title: Three-time world champion
facts.narration: Fact number fifteen! Pelé is the only player in history to win three World Cups. He won in nineteen fifty-eight, nineteen sixty-two, and nineteen seventy. No other player has ever done it!

facts.title: The Black Spider
facts.narration: Fact number sixteen! Lev Yashin, the legendary Soviet goalkeeper, is the only goalkeeper to ever win the Ballon d'Or. He won it in nineteen sixty-three. He always dressed in black, so fans called him the Black Spider!

facts.title: Hand of God
facts.narration: Fact number seventeen! In nineteen eighty-six, Diego Maradona scored two of the most famous goals ever, in the same match against England. First, he scored with his hand, the Hand of God! Just four minutes later, he dribbled past five players and scored the Goal of the Century!

facts.title: The psychic octopus
facts.narration: Fact number eighteen! At the twenty ten World Cup, an octopus named Paul predicted the winners of matches by choosing food from one of two boxes. He picked all seven of Germany's games and the final correctly. Eight out of eight! Paul the Octopus became a worldwide celebrity.

facts.title: The fastest World Cup goal
facts.narration: Fact number nineteen! The fastest goal in World Cup history was scored by Hakan Shukur of Turkey, in two thousand two. He scored against South Korea after just eleven seconds! Some fans hadn't even sat down yet!

facts.title: 5000 to 1
facts.narration: Fact number twenty! Before the twenty fifteen season, bookmakers gave Leicester City odds of five thousand to one to win the Premier League. Everyone thought they would fight to stay in the league. Instead, they won the title! It's one of the greatest surprises in sports history.

facts.title: The Invincibles
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-one! In the two thousand three, two thousand four season, Arsenal played all thirty-eight Premier League games without losing a single one. Twenty-six wins and twelve draws! That's why they're known as the Invincibles.

facts.title: Signed on a napkin
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-two! Lionel Messi's first agreement with Barcelona was written on a paper napkin when he was just thirteen years old. Years later, that napkin was sold at auction for more than seven hundred thousand pounds! The most valuable napkin in the world!

facts.title: 91 goals in one year
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-three! In twenty twelve, Lionel Messi scored ninety-one goals in a single year, for Barcelona and Argentina. That's a world record! That's almost two goals every single week for a whole year!

facts.title: Five World Cups, five goals
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-four! Cristiano Ronaldo was the first player in history to score at five different World Cups. He scored in two thousand six, twenty ten, twenty fourteen, twenty eighteen, and twenty twenty-two. What a legend!

facts.title: The craziest score ever
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-five! The craziest score in soccer history is one hundred forty-nine to zero! It happened in Madagascar in two thousand two. One team was so angry about a referee's decision that they kept scoring own goals on purpose, in protest. One hundred forty-nine own goals!
